title: Legacy TLS 1.0 Negotiated
description: Session negotiated TLS 1.0 which is deprecated by RFC 8996 due to known cryptographic weaknesses.
impact: Exposes traffic to eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks via BEAST, POODLE, and fallback exploits.
recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 on mail server and client configurations. Enforce TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3.

title: Legacy TLS 1.1 Negotiated
description: Session negotiated TLS 1.1 which is deprecated by RFC 8996 and lacks modern cipher support.
impact: Lacks support for modern authenticated encryption (AEAD) algorithms and weak key exchange.
recommendation: Disable TLS 1.1 on mail server and client configurations. Require minimum TLS 1.2.

title: Legacy CBC Cipher Suite Negotiated
description: Session negotiated a legacy Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) cipher suite under encryption.
impact: CBC mode ciphers in older TLS implementations are vulnerable to padding oracle attacks.
recommendation: Migrate cipher suite selection to AEAD suites such as AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

title: Weak Cipher Suite Negotiated
description: Session negotiated an inherently weak or broken cipher suite (NULL, EXPORT, RC4, DES, 3DES, MD5).
impact: Allows trivial decryption or authentication bypass by active network attackers.
recommendation: Remove weak ciphers from server cipher preference lists immediately.

title: Unencrypted Plaintext Email Session
description: Email session communicated over plaintext without TLS transport encryption.
impact: Email headers, commands, authentication credentials, and body contents are exposed to passive wiretapping.
recommendation: Enforce mandatory TLS/STARTTLS for all mail transport and access sessions.

title: STARTTLS Offered but Not Issued
description: Server advertised STARTTLS capability, but the client failed to issue STARTTLS and continued in plaintext.
impact: Session fell back to unencrypted transport despite server support for encryption.
recommendation: Configure mail client to enforce mandatory STARTTLS encryption (Opportunistic TLS upgrade).

title: STARTTLS Stripping or Downgrade Attack Detected
description: STARTTLS capability was stripped from server response or STARTTLS command failed with server error.
impact: Indicates active MITM adversary tampering with mail session capabilities to force plaintext fallback.
recommendation: Enable DANE (RFC 6698) or MTA-STS (RFC 8461) to enforce verified TLS connections.

title: Expired X.509 Certificate
description: Server TLS certificate expired before the time of the capture.
impact: Clients cannot establish trust in the server identity, exposing session to MITM impersonation.
recommendation: Renew server certificate immediately using automated certificate management (e.g. ACME / Let's Encrypt).

title: Certificate Not Yet Valid
description: Server certificate issue date (notBefore) is in the future relative to the capture start time.
impact: Certificate is invalid, causing TLS handshake errors or untrusted connection warnings.
recommendation: Verify system clock synchronization (NTP) on mail server and issue valid certificates.

title: Certificate Hostname Mismatch
description: Server certificate CN/SAN does not match the observed destination SNI or hostname.
impact: Subject identity validation failed; connection cannot verify server authenticity.
recommendation: Re-issue server certificate with proper Subject Alternative Names (SAN) matching mail server hostnames.

title: Weak Public Key Size (< 2048-bit RSA)
description: Server RSA certificate uses a key length under 2048 bits (e.g. 1024 bits).
impact: RSA 1024-bit keys offer insufficient security margin against factorization by well-funded adversaries.
recommendation: Re-key certificate with minimum RSA 2048-bit or ECDSA P-256 key.

title: Weak Certificate Signature Algorithm
description: Certificate signed using deprecated cryptographic hash algorithm (MD5 or SHA-1).
impact: Hash collision vulnerabilities allow attackers to forge valid-appearing certificates.
recommendation: Re-issue certificate signed with SHA-256 or stronger digest algorithm.

title: Plaintext Credentials Exposed on Network
description: User authentication credentials (AUTH LOGIN, USER/PASS) transmitted outside TLS encryption.
impact: Immediate exposure of username and cleartext password to network eavesdroppers.
recommendation: Enforce TLS encryption prior to permitting authentication commands; disable plaintext AUTH methods on port 25/110/143.

title: Modern TLS Version Negotiated
description: Session established using modern TLS protocol (TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3).
impact: Provides essential transport layer confidentiality and data integrity.
recommendation: Maintain minimum TLS version requirement at TLS 1.2.

title: Strong AEAD Cipher Suite with Forward Secrecy
description: Session uses modern authenticated encryption (AEAD) with ephemeral key exchange (ECDHE/DHE).
impact: Guarantees forward secrecy and authenticated encryption against eavesdropping.
recommendation: Continue prioritizing AEAD ciphers in server preference order.
